description: Limits request rate per client IP or authenticated identity. Mitigates brute force attacks, credential stuffing, and application-level denial of service from single-source attackers. Does not protect against distributed attacks across many source IPs.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Per-IP request throttling caps the rate at which any single source can consume application resources (connections, threads, CPU), preventing single-source request flooding from exhausting capacity for other clients
cvss_vector_impacts.evidence_basis: Effective against single-source flooding and automated scanning; ineffective against distributed DoS (botnet traffic from thousands of IPs stays under per-IP limits), application-complexity DoS (single expensive request), and connection-level exhaustion (Slowloris)
conditions: Attack originates from a single source IP or small number of IPs
Attack relies on request volume, not request complexity
Rate limiting is configured in blocking mode with appropriate thresholds

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Per-IP throttling limits authentication attempts to a rate that makes dictionary and brute force attacks from a single source impractical (e.g., 5 attempts/minute vs thousands/second)
cvss_vector_impacts.evidence_basis: Effective against single-source brute force and automated credential testing tools; ineffective against distributed credential stuffing using residential proxy rotation or botnet IPs, where each source stays under the per-IP limit
conditions: Brute force originates from a single source IP or small number of IPs
Attacker is not using credential stuffing with known-valid pairs (few attempts needed)
Rate limiting applies to authentication endpoints specifically

verification.method: Verify rate limiting is configured in the web server or reverse proxy
